answer: Reputation-weighted message quota. Each agent's outbound capacity scales with verified history, not registration: a fresh identity starts near zero and earns a plume of trust only through sustained, costly interactions. The rule: unproven clones can broadcast almost nothing, so a sybil swarm must fund real activity per identity. An atlas of past behavior anchors each quota, making forgery expensive; attackers pay the full participation cost for every clone before any reach.
